rich_summary: This section recounts the unusual births that secure the continuation of the Kuru lineage. When Vyasa approaches Ambalika for a second heir, she turns pale with fear at his austere appearance, and Vyasa foretells that her son will likewise be pale—Pandu, future father of the Pandavas. Later, a princess refuses another union with Vyasa and instead sends her maid, whose humility pleases the sage; their child becomes Vidura, famed for wisdom and justice. The narrative then shifts to the origin of Vidura’s divine aspect: the god of Justice (Dharma) was cursed to be born among humans after the unjust punishment of the ascetic Mandavya, who was wrongly impaled by royal officers pursuing thieves. The episode explores fate, moral justice, and the complex origins of key Kuru figures.

highlight_spans.why: Vyasa’s encounter with Ambalika and the prophecy explaining why her son will be called Pandu.
Ambalika’s fear and the emotional tension surrounding the conception of a future king.
The maid respectfully receives Vyasa and is blessed; this moment leads to the birth of Vidura, the embodiment of wisdom and justice.
The account of the ascetic Mandavya’s wrongful impalement, which sets up the curse that causes the god of Justice to be born as Vidura.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ambalika recoils in fear at the austere, wild-looking sage Vyasa inside the dim royal chamber as he foretells the birth of the pale prince Pandu.
A beautifully adorned maid respectfully greets Vyasa in the palace chamber, kneeling with humility while the sage blesses her future child, Vidura.
The ascetic Mandavya sits impaled upon a stake beneath a tree, still alive in deep meditation while other sages arrive at night in the forms of birds around him.
